subject: german

items.correct: All of them — every noun is capitalised.
items.why: Capitalising all nouns is a distinctive rule of German.

items.q: Do German nouns and articles change in different roles?
items.correct: Yes — German uses cases (nominative, accusative, dative, genitive).
items.why: The case changes articles and some endings depending on the noun's role.

items.q: Can you always guess a German noun's gender from its meaning?
items.correct: No — gender is often grammatical (das Mädchen, 'girl', is neuter).
items.misconception: Yes, meaning always tells you the gender.
items.why: Gender frequently has to be learned with the noun.

items.q: Do German adjective endings stay the same?
items.correct: No — they change with case, gender and number.
items.why: Adjective endings are a core part of German grammar.
